title: Stabilize SSE byte-stitcher and fncall ordinals to avoid mid-frame JSON corruption
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: We observed rare but repeatable user incidents where streaming responses terminated with partial JSON payloads or interleaved fncall tokens when the transport split occurred inside multi-byte UTF-8 sequences or when heartbeats and event payloads were coalesced. This caused downstream OpenAI-compat clients to error on parse or lose function call ordering. Summary: Introduce a conservative byte-stitcher that coalesces adjacent SSE chunks across transport boundaries, an escape-coalescer to avoid splitting JSON escape sequences, and an explicit ordinal watermark for function-call events so the tool/function-caller reconciler can re-order or re-emit lost events deterministically. The change is limited to the OpenAI-compat SSE emitter and the streaming parser path; it does not alter non-streaming API behavior.Design highlights: 1) SSE byte-stitcher: buffer up to 256 bytes across chunk boundaries when a chunk ends with an incomplete UTF-8 codepoint or an open JSON token (open quote, backslash, or unclosed brace). Stitcher emits a tight checksum (8-bit XOR) in a non-protocol header for local reassembly checks during dechunking. 2) Escape coalescer: detect trailing backslashes and ensure escape sequences (e.g., \uXXXX) are not split across writes. 3) Fncall ordinals: attach a monotonic ordinal to fncall sentinel events (X-Redwood-Fn-Ordinal header emitted inline as event detail) and a small resume-ack handshake that allows clients to request retransmit of ordinal ranges on reconnect. 4) Heartbeat slab adjuster: reduce heartbeat-induced coalescing by introducing a 10ms jitter in heartbeat emission when higher-priority fncall events are pacing through the emitter to avoid interleaving.5) Safety and performance tradeoffs: Default behavior is opt-in via server flag --sse-stitcher=enabled for rollout. Stitcher only engages for chunk sizes < 4KB and when a heuristic detects likely split. The checksum and ordinal metadata are intentionally tiny to limit overhead.Testing: Unit tests added for UTF-8 split cases, escaped unicode sequences, and fncall ordinal monotonicity. Integration tests simulated TCP-level fragmentation and reassembly using a faker transport; we replayed production captures that previously triggered the bug. Load test: end-to-end latency impact measured under production-like batching; median token latency increased ~0.3ms and P99 remained within SLOs. Rollout and migration: feature gate enabled in staged Canary for 48 hours in us-west-2, then expanded to 20% of traffic, monitored via new metric sse.stitcher.rescue_count and fncall.ordinal-mismatch. Backout plan: gate off and fall back to previous emitter; reconnect resumes without user-visible data loss (clients will see a small chance of duplicated fncall which is guarded by idempotency in the function-caller reconciler).
commit_summary: init: add sse byte-stitcher module with buffer and checksum logic
feat: introduce escape coalescer for trailing-backslash and \uXXXX sequences
feat: attach ordinal metadata to fncall sentinel events and add resume ack handler
chore: add unit and integration tests and faker transport for fragmented replay
perf: add heuristics to avoid stitcher on large chunks and add telemetry hooks
docs: document new feature-gate and rollout notes in sse.md
test: update e2e harness and add fragmented-capture fixture
changes_snippet: byte_stitcher.rs: add Stitcher::append_chunk(chunk: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> with XOR checksum appended as trailer
dechunker.rs: validate checksum when present and attempt local reassembly before failing parse
fncall_ordinal.rs: bump ordinal counter per-stream and emit X-Redwood-Fn-Ordinal as inline event attribute
escape_coalescer.rs: detect trailing '\\u' and '\\' sequences and buffer until completion
review_comments: Elliot Green: Can we make the stitcher threshold configurable per-tenant? Some high-throughput tenants may prefer lower latency than rescue coverage.
Maya Patel (author): Exposed as --sse-stitcher-threshold-ms and a per-tenant header override; documented in sse.md and default kept conservative.
Samir Choudhury: How do we avoid double-emitting fncalls after reconnect? Clients could receive duplicate ordinals.
Maya Patel (author): Added resume-ack handshake and recommend idempotent fncall handlers; reconciler now drops duplicate ordinals if payload checksum matches previously processed ordinal.

release_notes: Fix rare SSE stream truncation and fncall reordering by introducing a conservative byte-stitcher and ordinal metadata; opt-in via --sse-stitcher. Improved resilience to UTF-8 and escape sequence splits; minor median latency impact reported.
